answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake that grows with the number of identities it claims, like a saffron merchant paying a deposit per stall: the first stall is cheap, the tenth costs ten times more, so a zephyr of fake identities becomes prohibitively expensive. At the zenith of this curve, creating one more fake identity costs more than any transaction it could ever earn from, making mass fakery unprofitable while honest single agents stay nearly free.
